question.text: The time period of a simple pendulum is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><msqrt><mfrac><mi>l</mi><mi>g</mi></mfrac></msqrt><mo>.</mo></math> The measured value of the length of the pendulum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> known to a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> accuracy. The time for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn></math> oscillations of the pendulum is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> second using a clock of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> resolution. The percentage accuracy in the determination of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi></math> using this pendulum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> to the nearest integer is:-
